newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-HART CRITICISES TRI-NATIONS DRAW.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-HART CRITICISES TRI-NATIONS DRAW.

text.p: New Zealand coach John Hart criticised the Tri-Nations series schedule on Thursday saying the 1997 draw favoured South Africa.

"The draw needs to be revised because, at the moment, it is going to favour one side each year. This year, that side happens to be South Africa," Hart said after New Zealand flew into Johannesburg to prepare for their opening match against the Springboks on July 19.
New Zealand, Australia and South Africa play each other both home and away in a competition which effectively decides the champions of the southern hemisphere.
"It is a one-sided draw in terms of the travelling and the travel factor will continue to determine the series.
"To expect us to play South Africa in Johannesburg at altitude and then, one week later, to play in front of 100,000 people against Australia in Melbourne is an impossible ask."
Hart suggested that a bye should be placed into the middle of the Tri-Nations series schedule when no team would play.

"In this way, you would avoid the situation where teams travel in or out of South Africa a week apart - that's a real killer. At this stage, any team coming in or out of South Africa is badly disadvantaged and has an enormous obstacle to overcome."
Hart said it would be vital to draw first blood in the series when the All Blacks take on the Springboks at Ellis Park on Saturday week.
"To draw first blood in Johannesburg will be awfully important because not many teams win away in the Tri-Nations - that's what makes it such a difficult competition."
While not surprised by the professionalism of the victorious 1997 British Lions, Hart said South Africa should have won their recent three-match series against Martin Johnson's men.
"I wasn't surprised with the success of the British Lions. The game of rugby today is all about selection and professional management and that Lions' squad were supremely well prepared.

"But, conversely, I thought South Africa should have won the series 2-1, if not 3-0. The present Springbok side is a step-up from what we saw last year and a new pattern is emerging. I think this 1997 South African side is a better side than the one in 1996."
